memory_update.text: US-listed pure-play CTC/HVDC transformer winding component exposure appears limited; the best direct CTC suppliers identified in external context are non-US or not straightforwardly US-listed, including KSH International, ASTA Energy Solutions, and Essex/Superior Essex via LS Group.
GPC should be tracked as a hidden large-cap wrapper for EIS/Motion transformer OEM materials exposure, but evidence must separate value-added transformer inputs from generic industrial distribution.

PLPC is not a transformer winding component supplier, but it is a small-cap, narrow transmission-hardware candidate for the same grid buildout procurement cycle and may fit a second-order underfollowed lane.
GE Vernova is a useful reference anchor because ASTA has disclosed CTC supply to GE Vernova transformer sites; use it to map upstream suppliers rather than as the primary underfollowed candidate.
AMSC belongs in speculative_shadow only: it has qualified grid-input characteristics through HTS wire and REG systems, but no verified exposure to conventional HVDC transformer winding CTC.

node: HVDC transformer winding components, continuously transposed conductors, and qualified grid-OEM inputs
summary: US-listed direct pure-plays in HVDC transformer winding components appear scarce. The clearest public-market mapping is therefore a two-lane universe: reference OEMs that buy qualified CTC and transformer inputs, plus underfollowed US-listed second-order suppliers and distributors around transformer manufacturing, grid hardware, and qualified grid inputs. GE Vernova is included only as a reference anchor because it is a large HVDC/power-transformer OEM and disclosed customer of ASTA CTC. The underfollowed lane includes Genuine Parts via hidden EIS/Motion exposure to transformer OEM materials, Preformed Line Products as a narrow transmission hardware supplier benefiting from grid buildout but not directly CTC, and American Superconductor as a speculative adjacent qualified-grid-input candidate through HTS wire/grid systems rather than conventional transformer winding CTC.
